newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: India attacked at global telecoms negotiations.
newsitem.headline: India attacked at global telecoms negotiations.

text.p: The EU chief negotiator to global telecommunications talks in Geneva criticised India on Wednesday for dragging its feet on liberalisation of its international telephone charges.
Karl Falkenberg said the EU was worried about India's discrimination against different countries regarding charges on international calls in its proposal submitted to the talks.
He said India was insisting on applying Most Favoured Nation status to accounting rate systems for international calls and was the only country among the negotiating partners to do so.
India was still using the old system under which accounting rates are negotiated and fixed for different routes, he added.

"They are protecting their accounting rate system. They charge different rates for calls from the United States or Europe," he told reporters. "This is a factor of disturbance. We don't think they are justified."
The talks in Geneva on a global pact to decontrol the $600 billion world telecommunications market are scheduled to finish ahead of a Saturday deadline.
